Bánh Mì 37 Nguyễn Trãi: Delicious and Affordable
Oct 2024 • Friends
Bánh Mì 37 Nguyễn Trãi is a must-visit spot for anyone craving a great Bánh Mì. The sandwiches here are packed with flavor, thanks to the crispy, freshly baked baguette and tasty fillings. The pork is tender and perfectly grilled, and the pickled veggies and herbs add the right amount of crunch and freshness.

The shop is small and casual, but it's always lively. It’s perfect for a quick bite on the go, and the prices are really good for the quality you get.

The service is quick and friendly, even when it's busy. They also offer chili and sauces if you like a bit of heat.

If you're in the area and want a tasty, filling meal that won’t break the bank, Bánh Mì 37 Nguyễn Trãi is the place to go. Highly recommended!

Tasty healthier banh mi (no pate in this version)
Jul 2024 • Couples
This was a cheap eat, priced very well for a good banh mi. They were 28,000 Vietnamese dong each.

The banh mi has grilled pork, chilli, herbs, cucumber. There is no pate or cold cuts in this version, so we are calling it the ‘healthier’ banh mi. 

We liked that the two women grill the pork on the grill and the queue moves quickly.

We would recommend, however we preferred the ‘unhealthy’ banh mi from Huynh hoa which contained cold cuts and a ridiculous amount of pate. It depends what you prefer.

An institution since 1980
Apr 2024 • Solo
Tasty and filling banh mi but underwhelming bread. I live in France and I normally find the bread in Vietnam is of an equally high standard, but today's, although visually appealing, lacked in structure and freshness. The filling, on the other hand, was exceptional, and I quickly realised why there was such a long line (of mostly Vietnamese) to obtain such tasty morsels. The homemade freshly grilled pork patties are flavoursome, but once coupled with the shredded daikon and carrot, salad leaves, cucumber wedge, chilli seeds and special sauce become more than their sum of parts. The sauce brings everything together. It is kind of like a barbecue sauce, I suspect made with a soy sauce base, but it has a ketchup sweetness and consistency that made me think of tamarind and dates. The cart is old and beaten up, it is probably the original from when the stand first opened in 1980. The old lady assembling the banh mi works dexterously with expert hands. The bread rolls were opened with scissor, before she placed five pork patties in each along with the affor mentioned accompaniments. A steal at 28,000 dong, which is €1.13 at today's exchange rate. A small motorcycle delivered a fresh basket of rolls moments after mine was made, so I will give Banh Mi 37 another go tomorrow and hopefully get a fresher roll. All in all, it was a cheap and satisfying meal and worth the hourlong walk from where I am staying in Japantown area of District 1. Don't be put off by the wait, your taste buds will thank you for it.

There was a large crowd surrounding it so I decided to buy a Banh Mi. I've had a few Banh Mi while in HCMC and this was one of the best. What makes it so good is the freshly grilled BBQ pork patties. They grill the pork right next to the cart so its very fresh. The sauce used is also different from some that I've had in the city. For 30,000VND it is definitely worth the price.

I was told Saigon cuisine
Dec 2019
I was told Saigon cuisine tends to be on the sweet side. Got that 5 before 4pm their opening time, get to watch how these ladies prepare for the long queue. Grill lady: Skillfully flipping those freshly made meat patty on the grill, and browning it, must have kind of some honey inside. Banh mi maker and cashier two in one, carries out a jar of their secret ingredient sauce, the rest is pretty much standard, radish pickles, cilantros, cucumber. Their hot sauce is on the mild side. Would be nicer if they can have an option for some hot green chili to give it a kick. 

Like it better than those banh mi with processed meats.
